v.q: How does kind run a Kubernetes cluster?
o: Each node is a Docker container running systemd, containerd and Kubernetes
Each node is a virtual machine started by a hypervisor
The control plane runs as a process on your host without any container
Nodes are Pods scheduled on a remote cloud cluster
v.w: kind stands for Kubernetes IN Docker: node containers bootstrapped with kubeadm. It needs only Docker.

v.q: Which statement about how kind runs a cluster is NOT true?
o: Each node is a full virtual machine
Each node is a Docker container
Nodes run containerd inside
The cluster starts in about a minute
v.w: kind runs nodes as containers that share the host kernel. Virtual machines are what minikube drivers or VM tools use.

v.q: A Pod using an image you just built locally ends in ErrImagePull on kind. What is the most likely fix?
o: Run kind load docker-image so the nodes have the image
Restart the Docker daemon on the host
Change the Service type to LoadBalancer
Delete the namespace and create it again
v.w: The nodes have their own container runtime and cannot see host images. Load the image (or use a local registry) and use a fixed tag.

v.q: Which command makes a locally built image available to the nodes?
o: kind load docker-image
docker push to localhost
kubectl apply -f image
kubectl pull image
v.w: The nodes are containers with their own image store, so a host image must be loaded into them.

v.q: Why avoid the latest tag for locally loaded images?
o: Kubernetes then defaults to imagePullPolicy Always and pulls from a registry
The latest tag is not allowed by kind and is rejected at creation time
Docker deletes local images tagged latest after about one hour of idle time
Services cannot select Pods that use the latest tag in their image field
v.w: With a fixed tag the default policy is IfNotPresent, which uses the loaded image.

v.q: A Pod uses image myapp:latest, loaded into kind, but it is pulled from a registry. What setting causes this?
o: imagePullPolicy defaults to Always for latest
imagePullPolicy defaults to Never
kind forbids the latest tag
The Service type is wrong
v.w: For the latest tag Kubernetes defaults to Always. Use a fixed tag or set imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent.

v.q: How can a kind cluster publish ports 80 and 443 to your host?
o: extraPortMappings in the kind config, plus an ingress controller
Running kubectl proxy as a background service
Setting hostNetwork on every Deployment
Nothing is needed, kind publishes all node ports by default
v.w: kind does not publish node ports by default. Configure extraPortMappings on a node and install ingress-nginx, or use kubectl port-forward.

v.q: Which is needed to reach an ingress controller on port 80 of the host in kind?
o: extraPortMappings in the cluster config
hostNetwork on every Deployment
A cloud load balancer
Nothing, kind publishes everything
v.w: The node is a container, so a port mapping publishes its port to the host.

v.q: Why does a LoadBalancer Service stay Pending on kind?
o: There is no cloud controller to create a load balancer
kind blocks the LoadBalancer type in its admission rules
The Service has no selector
The node image is too old
v.w: Install MetalLB or cloud-provider-kind to assign external IPs locally.

v.q: Which add-on can give LoadBalancer Services an address in a kind cluster?
o: MetalLB
kube-proxy
CoreDNS
etcd
v.w: kind has no cloud controller, so the Service stays Pending unless a load balancer implementation is installed.

v.q: Which use is kind best suited for?
o: Disposable clusters in CI to test manifests, charts and operators
Running a production banking platform on a single laptop
Measuring the performance of a production workload
Hosting a shared team cluster with high availability and cloud storage
v.w: kind is fast and disposable but single-host, resource-bound and without cloud features.

v.q: Which use is NOT a good fit for kind?
o: Production customer traffic
Testing a Helm chart in CI
Testing an operator
Trying a new manifest
v.w: kind clusters are disposable and not designed for production, high availability or persistent cloud storage.

v.q: What is the main difference between kind and minikube?
o: kind runs nodes as containers for tests and CI; minikube uses drivers and addons
kind runs only on Linux hosts while minikube runs only on macOS laptops
kind is meant for production clusters while minikube is only for learning
kind uses its own Kubernetes fork that has different APIs from upstream
v.w: Both run real Kubernetes. minikube adds addons, dashboard and tunnel; kind is lighter and easier for multi-node and CI.

v.q: Which statement about kind and minikube is NOT true?
o: kind is meant for production use
kind starts nodes as containers
minikube has addons
Both run real Kubernetes
v.w: Both are local tools. Neither is a production platform.

v.q: Why pin the kindest/node image version?
o: It fixes the Kubernetes version, so tests match what production runs
It determines how many nodes the cluster can have
It selects the CNI plugin used for pod networking
It sets the Docker version used on the host
v.w: Testing on a different minor version can hide removed APIs or changed defaults.

v.q: Which line pins the Kubernetes version of a kind node?
o: image: kindest/node:v1.30.0
version: 1.30
driver: docker
runtime: containerd
v.w: The node image contains the Kubernetes release, so a fixed tag keeps the version the same on every machine.
